items.title: Ray Brown interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, AZ, April 16, 2000
items.q: I worked with Lalo Schifrin. We did all of — that show that was so famous he did

ctx.x: Every day something different or did you get like maybe longer term contracts for T.V. shows and things?

Well the most interesting work is the movies, because a guy writes a score for a movie, so even if you work for let’s say Johnny Mandel on four different pictures, all the music © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

is different. But they were now in the throes of trying jazz composers, you know, people who were associated with jazz because they were getting more interesting music — music that — they were making deals, they started putting out albums. Sometimes the albums, the music would sell the picture. So they had people like Quincy Jones and Henry Mancini, Johnny Mandel, and Oliver Nelson and Michel LeGrand, a bunch of people associated with jazz music. And these people would hire orchestras but they had jazz musicians…
